name: Josip Broz Tito
role: Yugoslav Partisan leader, prime minister (1943-1963) and president of Yugoslavia (1953-1980)
summary: A Marxist-Leninist who led the Partisan uprising and then a one-party socialist federation, nationalised industry and redistributed land, and after the 1948 break with Stalin developed workers' self-management and non-alignment. He backed national equality within Yugoslavia and decentralisation, opposed colonialism and Soviet dominance, and ruled through party control, repressing dissent and nationalist movements.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1958 programme he led lists protection in case of illness as a right of working people under social ownership, with health services run by social bodies; no explicit statement on universal coverage.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called capitalist commodity production anarchic and planned heavy industrialisation, though in later years he accepted markets and competition between self-managed enterprises inside socialism.

public-ownership.rationale: Reported that his government nationalised factories, mines, transport, large estates and all trade, and said no enterprise of public character remained in private hands.

unions-good.rationale: Described trade unions as having an important role in training workers and, under socialism, a great role; in 1950 he said their protective function would weaken once workers manage firms.

property-fundamental.rationale: Led the confiscation of enemy and capitalist property, the Basic Law on Expropriation and nationalisation of private enterprises, and defended these as the foundation of socialism.

cut-welfare.rationale: His government created state-backed insurance for workers and their families and the programme he led expands social services; he never argued that welfare breeds dependency.

worker-ownership.rationale: Presented "factories for the workers" as the goal and gave workers' councils management powers, but described the result as social ownership by the whole community rather than ownership by each firm's workers.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Cited the Law Prohibiting Incitement of National, Racial or Religious Hatreds, with strict punishment, as proof his state was socialist and not fascist.

state-harmful.rationale: Said the proletariat needs a state in the transition and that Yugoslavia kept one to restrain exploiters, while holding that it should gradually wither away.

empower-police-military.rationale: Said Yugoslavia built a powerful military force at heavy sacrifice because independence was threatened, though he criticised growth of Soviet police organs.

decide-locally.rationale: Carried out and defended decentralisation of economic ministries to republics, districts, communes and workers' collectives, calling it democratic and a step in the withering of state functions.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme describes socialism as abolishing patriarchal family legislation and giving the family a new basis; it does not treat the traditional family as society's foundation.

more-religion-public.rationale: An atheist who led a party whose programme speaks of freeing minds from religious narcosis; the state curbed church property and influence, though from the mid-1950s he relaxed restrictions.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He promoted healthy socialist patriotism, and the programme he led aims at the intensive development of the cultures of the Yugoslav peoples.

gradual-change.rationale: Led a revolution that destroyed the old state apparatus and expropriated owners, but held that the state and central management should wither gradually rather than in leaps.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Said Yugoslav policy follows the UN Charter and that the UN would achieve far more if universal and freed of veto and bloc division, without proposing new powers for it.

nation-first.rationale: Argued that socialist patriotism is internationalist, that narrow national or state interest is the test of nationalism, and that Yugoslavia favours active cooperation with other states.

revolution-justified.rationale: Led the 1941 uprising and the social revolution that followed and defended the revolutionary destruction of the old state machine as consistent with Marxism.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rejected doubts that workers could master factory management, calling distrust of them blindness to their creative abilities, though he stressed training and specialists.

central-planning.rationale: Praised the Five Year Plan and central direction while the country was devastated, but later called centralised management a brake and decentralised toward self-management.

socialized-markets.rationale: Yugoslav self-management operated within commodity production and money; in 1957 he criticised disloyal competition between enterprises, accepting that enterprises compete.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Drove the Five Year Plan for industrialisation and electrification, with state-directed building of factories and railways in backward regions.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wanted peasants to shed "small-owner" habits and move into socialist cooperatives and large-scale socialised production.

one-party-rule.rationale: Led a one-party state, defended it against Western criticism and called multiparty politics "squabbling"; the programme asserts the leading role of the Communist Party in government.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Proclaimed a federal people's republic, denounced the king and the royal government in exile as reaction, and spoke harshly of the Karadjordjevic monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Praised democracy but defined it as workers' management on a material basis, calling multiparty Western democracy formal; the regime allowed no free choice of rulers.

workers-councils.rationale: Gave directly elected workers' councils management of enterprises, but did not replace the Federal Assembly with them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Said every Yugoslav nationality had a right of self-determination including secession and that none chose to use it, yet he suppressed nationalist movements in practice.

political-violence-never.rationale: Called for armed uprising against the occupiers and collaborators and wrote the Partisan oath to fight until the enemy was annihilated.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred: his regime and programme were secular and Marxist, with law from the socialist state.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Built a federation of equal nationalities, condemned national chauvinism and hegemony of one group, and called brotherhood and unity the base of the state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: His speeches and the programme treat history as the struggle of classes, with class struggle continuing under construction of socialism.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Said the interests of the individual must coincide with those of the whole socialist community and criticised localism and the "principle of the stronger".

duties-before-rights.rationale: Warned that individual interests must coincide with community interests, but the programme he led also insists personal rights cannot wait for a later stage of socialism.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Treated industrialisation and electrification as the material basis of socialism and a source of national wealth.

restore-past-order.rationale: Called for building a new socialist order and criticised stereotypes and dogmatism, and the revolution he led abolished the monarchy and old class order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said practical results are the best proof of the self-management system and that Marxism is a guide for orientation, not a dogma.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Quoted Marx approvingly that the higher phase of communism distributes by need, while saying Yugoslavia and the USSR were far from it; his own system paid by work.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme says socialism replaces the capitalist craving for profit with society's effort to satisfy personal and collective needs.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described capitalist managers as squeezing profit out of workers, and defined nationalisation as laying the foundation for ending the exploitation of man by man.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said the new Yugoslav state restrains the minority of exploiters and the programme calls the working-class government a specific form of the dictatorship of the proletariat.

collective-farming.rationale: His government carried out an early cooperative drive and a land reform, but the programme he led makes entry into socialist cooperatives voluntary and leaves private peasant holdings.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The programme keeps the thesis that imperialism engenders crises and war, but says a new world war is no longer inevitable.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Defended equal rights of nationalities and smaller national groups as collective entities, alongside personal rights in the programme.

conscription.rationale: Created the Yugoslav People's Army from the Partisan forces as a national force for defence; no separate statement on conscription.

positive-liberty.rationale: Argued that democracy rests on a material basis and the programme says personal rights need a social-economic foundation and cannot be postponed.

total-state.rationale: Held that the state should wither and the programme urges freeing education, science and the arts from administrative interference.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Listed the desire for foreign conquest and oppression of other nations as negative traits of nationalism, and said wars of conquest are never justified.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In 1967 he proposed that Arab states recognise Israel in exchange for return of newly occupied territory (secondhand report).

workplace-democracy.rationale: Introduced the law giving workers' collectives elected councils that approve plans, elect and recall management boards and distribute accumulation.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said every nationality of Yugoslavia has a right to self-determination, and welcomed the right of Asian and African peoples to settle their own affairs.

class-collaboration.rationale: Treated employers as an exploiting class to be expropriated and workers as the ruling class, with no partnership between them.

dominated-front.rationale: Said Yugoslavia opposes blocs and that its ties with India and Burma are not a third bloc, though he supported anti-colonial peoples.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme he led says socialism abolished patriarchal family legislation and promotes equal rights for women.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The programme says no discrimination exists in a national, religious or racial respect, and he denounced racism as fascist.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said the state is a product of class conflict and the bourgeois state is an apparatus of force in the hands of a minority.

national-mission.rationale: Stated that Yugoslavia has no intention of imposing its system on anyone and that each country builds socialism as conditions permit.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ran a state that owned industry, planned the economy, and ran social insurance, education and welfare.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme secures full equality before the law and no discrimination, and he stressed equality of nations and nationalities.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Argued Lenin allowed building socialism in one country and said it was quite possible in Yugoslavia.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Rejected Stalin's thesis that the state must grow stronger under capitalist encirclement and called it a pretext for centralism and bureaucracy.

population-transfer.rationale: Wikipedia reports that the Partisan leadership decided in 1944 to expel ethnic Germans and confiscate their property; his own statements are not given and he is contested on scope.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Led armed uprising and expropriation of owners and said methods are justified by social need, though he said aggression is not a method of spreading revolution.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Condemned national egoism and a desire to dominate other nations, and criticised the "principle of the stronger" among enterprises.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The 1974 constitution he championed bans organisations aimed at restoring capitalist relations, and after 1945 he ordered collaborators dealt with severely.

vanguard-party.rationale: Credited the Communist Party with leading the workers' revolution, destroying factions to make it the vanguard, and said its role is leader and educator of the working class.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Held that a multinational Yugoslavia achieved unity and strength through equal rights of its nationalities, not by suppressing difference.

party-controls-media.rationale: Presided over party-controlled media and in 1971 conceded that the party had lost control of the media, then moved against Croatian outlets.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Attacked factionalism in the party from the 1920s, called the destruction of fractions the condition of party unity and accused Trotskyists of splitting it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Inferred: an atheist Marxist who curbed church influence and ran a secular party state.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Held the presidency from 1953 until death, was re-elected repeatedly and was named president for life under the 1974 constitution.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Condemned disparagement of other nations' history and culture, and insisted on equality of the cultures of Yugoslav nationalities.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme requires unhampered development of national languages, and Wikipedia reports large-scale Albanian-language primary education in Kosovo under him.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Argued that underdeveloped countries should receive material and technical aid free of political conditions, benefiting donors as well.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: His reported 1967 proposal had Israel return newly occupied land for Arab recognition, the reverse of the statement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Abolished private ownership of the means of production but kept personal ownership of goods; the statement is a weaker claim than his own.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He said Soviet leaders had a bureaucratic caste and an imperialist policy yet called the USSR a socialist country despite its leaders' mistakes, though also saying state ownership is the lowest form of social ownership.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: His land reform took land from the church and Archbishop Stepinac was jailed in 1946, but from 1953-54 he relaxed restrictions and signed a 1966 agreement with the Holy See.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Served at once as president and as leader of the League of Communists, holding the final word on major decisions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: an atheist who denounced the monarchy; the cult of personality he tolerated was secular.

leader-cult.rationale: The programme condemns the cult of personality as a product of bureaucracy, yet his own rule featured large public portraits, mass cheers and palaces.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Said unity based on socialist awareness is not complete while class struggle continues, and warned of bureaucracy and revisionism among Soviet leaders.

land-redistribution.rationale: Reported an agrarian reform leaving rich peasants at most 25 hectares and distributing about 700,000 hectares to poor and landless peasants.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Demanded Istria, Trieste and parts of Carinthia partly because Slovenes and Croats inhabited them, alongside historic and national rights.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pursued South Slav unity, an alliance with Albania and planned closer union with Bulgaria; his 1948 speech called unification of socialist countries a long process.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The programme and his speeches support national cultures developing through their own institutions, as in Albanian-language schooling in Kosovo.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Argued socialism could be built only with material conditions of industry and cultural level, and the programme explains social change through productive forces.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Favoured integration of nations, economic cooperation and trade with the West and the East, not an autarkic bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Appealed to self-sacrifice and socialist consciousness but his system paid wages by work and in 1957 sought a better wage system.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Launched the 1941 uprising on his own judgement but said no insurrection can succeed without mass participation of the working class.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolished the monarchy and presided over a state that ended the old royal and class privileges.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Called colonial enslavement negative and unjustifiable, and condemned colonialism as one of four evils threatening humanity.

patriotic-education.rationale: Held that a healthy socialist patriotism should be fostered in the people and received Pioneer delegations, though no direct statement on school curricula.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The programme says state intervention can delay crises but cannot save capitalism.

delink-world-market.rationale: Argued underdeveloped countries should receive aid and be integrated into cooperation, not isolated.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The programme requires equal rights and no discrimination, and he banned incitement of hatred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Replaced hereditary monarchy with a republic whose head was chosen by the assembly; he denounced monarchy as reaction.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The programme says monopoly capitalism widened the gulf between developed and underdeveloped countries, and he said the Soviets exploited weaker states through trade terms.

party-own-road.rationale: Insisted that every country and party must find its own road to socialism and criticised Moscow's dictation.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Said Yugoslavia must rely on itself, but he accepted Western aid in the 1950s and urged aid to underdeveloped countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Listed the unjust loss of territories at the end of the First World War, such as Istria, the Slovene Littoral and Trieste, as rights Yugoslavia must realise.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Presented the liberation war as the foundation of the new Yugoslavia and said the constitution legalised its achievements.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Treated fascism as the enemy that the revolution defeated and rejected the charge that his own system was fascist.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Called Yugoslav socialist democracy a new kind different from Western formal democracy and urged each country to choose its own road.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Wikipedia reports covert Yugoslav help to liberation movements against the Portuguese empire and training of SWAPO and PAC activists.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Opposed interference in internal affairs and, in 1968, the Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia, though he accepted the Soviet intervention in Hungary in 1956.

non-intervention.rationale: Said Yugoslavia opposes any interference in other states' internal affairs and called it a source of infringement and division into spheres of influence.

religious-nation.rationale: Called for a front of all nationalities regardless of political or religious belief and ran a multi-religious federation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rejected Soviet leadership and "unreachable authorities", insisting on equality between states.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Said Slovenia, Croatia and Serbia help the poorer republics of Macedonia, Montenegro and Bosnia as much as possible through the plan and budgets.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The programme says personal ownership of consumer goods is an essential personal right that socialism protects and extends.

defeat-communism.rationale: Led a communist party and state and urged active coexistence between systems rather than defeating either.

religion-illusion.rationale: The programme says the struggle for socialism frees consciousness from naive faith and religious narcosis, though the state also granted religious freedom.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The programme says capitalism developed productive forces and the world market, creating a basis for socialism, while being now outdated.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programme credits the socialist economy and social institutions with the economic emancipation of women.

socialized-care.rationale: The programme says social technical base for housekeeping and institutions for child welfare free the family from backward housework.

majority-settlement.rationale: Wikipedia reports he banned the return of Serb colonists to Kosovo after 1945.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Held that Marxism-Leninism, applied to local conditions, was the basis of his road and called revisionism the target.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His regime jailed Informbiro suspects on Goli Otok, arrested Djilas, and in 1971 purged the Croatian leadership.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned colonial enslavement and colonial policy that kept countries from developing.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Promoted workers' self-management and direct participation of working people in running production and distribution.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: an atheist whose authority claimed to derive from the people and working class.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said Yugoslavia built a strong army as the means of defence and that the army would be the last function of the state to wither.

rich-first.rationale: His 1948 speech stresses speeding up the poorest republics through help from richer ones rather than letting some grow first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Declared that Yugoslavia belongs to no bloc, opposes military blocs and would join no war unless attacked.

racial-franchise.rationale: Built a multinational federation of equal peoples and opposed racism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Backed the 1971 and 1974 changes creating a rotating collective presidency with seats for each republic and province.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His government established state social insurance and welfare for workers and children.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The programme says socialism abolishes patriarchal family law and provides a new basis for relations between spouses.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Held that Yugoslavia must not let anyone interfere in its internal affairs or tie it to a bloc, and the programme condemns foreign bases.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The programme he led says work should be the only criterion of economic status and distribution follows work performed.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Led the Partisan war, wrote an oath to fight invaders to the end, and said Yugoslavia would fight if attacked.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Said no national group may impose economic exploitation on another and the republics aid each other.

independent-unions.rationale: Said unions should work under the leadership of the Party and train workers to socialist consciousness.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Held that without turning factories over to workers' management the Soviet system lacked a characteristic socialist measure and gave workers no say.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nationalised enterprises, hotels and sanatoriums and said health and social services should be run by social bodies.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Said the Yugoslav army serves only defence and would never be used for aggression, and that Yugoslavia would go to war only if attacked.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Said the Cominform resolution attacked the unity of Yugoslavia's peoples and called for civil war and dissolution, a charge directed at Soviet-bloc leaders.

arms-reduction.rationale: The programme and his speeches condemn the arms race and call for stopping it, while holding that Yugoslavia needed an army for defence.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Ordered in May 1945 that all armed formations outside the Yugoslav Army be disarmed immediately.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Attacked Trotskyists for spreading pacifism and opposition to resisting fascist conquest.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Condemned inequality between states and said underdeveloped countries should be given trade and aid on equal terms.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Reported that the Partisans put an end to the old state machine and built a new people's apparatus rather than taking over the old one.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Said in the old Yugoslavia national oppression by the Serbian clique meant economic exploitation of the oppressed peoples.

workers-own-party.rationale: Told an interviewer that new working-class organisations independent of Moscow should be built in capitalist countries.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Dismissed multiparty electoral politics as squabbling and said democracy rests on material control by producers.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme says equal rights for women in Yugoslavia are settled and women took part fully in the war and new state.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: an atheist Marxist, so unlikely to hold scripture inerrant.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Called for resisting restoration of capitalism and for defending the planned, nationalised socialist state.

national-church-status.rationale: Clashed with the Catholic church from 1945, when Archbishop Stepinac was jailed, and the state gave no church a privileged legal status.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Wikipedia reports he strongly backed the 1974 constitution that gave Kosovo and Vojvodina autonomous provinces.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: He banned Serb colonists from returning to Kosovo, according to Wikipedia, limiting outside settlement in a region of an ethnic minority.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Demanded protection and annexation for Slovene and Croat populations in Venezia Giulia and Carinthia, and protested their persecution.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Ruled through the Communist Party and stressed party unity and discipline.

national-resource-control.rationale: Reported nationalisation of mines and enterprises, with none left in foreign hands, and rejected economic subjugation by foreign states.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Said socialist patriotism is internationalist at heart and that building the country serves working people.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Led a communist-led system where the programme says commodity production and money distribution operate under socialism.

notes: Early postwar policy (1945-1952) was orthodox Leninist and repressive, including the Goli Otok camp and an early cooperative drive; after 1950 he promoted self-management, decentralisation, relaxed church policy and non-alignment. Answers use his mature positions where they differ, and the 1958 party programme is cited as a document he led, corroborated by his own speeches where possible. His 1961 Belgrade Non-Aligned speech and the 1948 CPY report text could not be fetched in full; the 1948 report is used from translated extracts.
